title: Avoid These 2 Common Tax Filing Mistakes: Bank Interest & LTCG
description: Many taxpayers incorrectly assume that income with TDS deducted or tax-exempt capital gains do not need to be reported in their Income Tax Return (ITR). Omitt.

faq.q: Do I need to report bank interest if TDS has already been deducted?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. TDS is only a part payment of your tax liability. You must report the *gross* interest income in your ITR, and then claim credit for the TDS deducted.

faq.q: My Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) from equity are below ₹1 lakh, so they are exempt. Do I still need to report them?
faq.a: Yes, even if your LTCG from equity or equity-oriented mutual funds is exempt (up to ₹1 lakh under Section 112A), you must still report the full amount in Schedule 112A of your ITR. Non-reporting can lead to mismatches with your AIS.

faq.q: What is the Annual Information Statement (AIS) and why is it important?
faq.a: AIS is a comprehensive statement provided by the Income Tax Department that consolidates all financial information related to a taxpayer, including interest, dividends, securities transactions, and more. It is crucial because the department uses this data for cross-verification with your ITR.

faq.q: What happens if there's a mismatch between my ITR and AIS/Form 26AS?
faq.a: A mismatch can trigger an intimation notice under Section 143(1) or even a scrutiny notice. You would then need to explain the discrepancy and provide supporting documents, which can be time-consuming and stressful.

faq.q: Can I revise my ITR if I realise I've missed reporting some income?
faq.a: Yes, if you discover an error or omission after filing your original ITR, you can file a revised return under Section 139(5) of the Income Tax Act. This can usually be done up to 31st December of the assessment year, or before the completion of assessment, whichever is earlier.

faq.q: Is interest from a savings account also considered taxable income?
faq.a: Yes, interest earned from a savings account is taxable under the head "Income from Other Sources." While Section 80TTA allows a deduction of up to ₹10,000 for such interest, the gross amount must first be reported in your ITR.
